title: HELP-LLM: Assessment of patient and caregiver safety in lay caregiver interactions with large language models (LLMs) during a video-based simulated out-of-hospital pediatric airway obstruction
summary: The aim of this study is to explore the interaction between humans and machines in a simulated emergency (video demonstration from a Pediatric Advanced Life Support (PALS) course). On the one hand, the “prompts” (inputs) of laypersons are to be exploratively and qualitatively recorded, as well as the quality of the outputs of the LLM, with professional assessment of patient safety of the human-machine interaction. For this purpose, approximately. 20-30 teachers and educators will be placed in a simulated setting, and their interaction with the LLM will be observed in three different simulated situations.
conditions: A simulated lay rescuer situation in the context of respiratory distress in pseudo-croup/croup is examined, which transitions into a resuscitation situation and then, after (simulated) stabilization, into team aftercare.

interventions.name: In this study, educational professionals are presented with three simulated child emergency situations in which they represent a third person from a (fictitious) team of three. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age of majority 
- Consent to the study
- Completed 3-year vocational training (educator, curative education) or completed studies to become a primary or secondary school teacher
- Sufficient knowledge of German (at least C1)
Exclusion criteria:
- Rejection of the study 
- Completed medical or nursing professional training of more than 3 years
